messages:
Maya Li: Quick heads-up — after the eu-west canary we saw a p99 spike when requests fell back to other regions. Noticed at ~14:08 UTC.
Raj Patel: Numbers? p95/p99 and which route caused fallback?
Maya Li: p95 stayed ~90ms, p99 jumped from 420ms -> 1.3s for eu-west tenants that hit fallback to us-east replicas. Throughput steady.
Henry Gomez: Pulled a few traces. Kernel selection flipped to the generic quantized path during fallback for seq_len=128. Stack trace shows kernel_swap at runtime -> heavy single-token kernel.
Olivia Park: Also saw KV cache hit-rate drop from 93% -> 64% across those sessions. Fanout to remote region amplifies KV miss amplification.
infra-bot: [alert] route-fallback-triggered eu-west -> us-east (count=124) | avg_extra_hop=220ms
Raj Patel: So two effects: extra network hop + worse kernel/exec path = p99 amplification. Any batching changes in canary?
Henry Gomez: We increased microbatch cap from 8 -> 16 to improve throughput during canary. That reduced per-token overhead but queuing added tail for small interactive requests.
Maya Li: Right — classic latency SLO vs throughput tradeoff. Microbatch=16 helped throughput but made rare long queues when fallback added 200ms network tail.
Lex Chen: Proposal: add routing affinity for cold KV keys (prefer local if kvcache_hit_rate < 80%) and keep microbatch cap per-route adaptive. If fallback occurs, force microbatch=4 for that route to prioritize latency.
Olivia Park: Preferring local for hot keys helps but we still need a fallback policy for capacity storms. Could we detect kernel-compat mismatch early and prefer compatible model variant on fallback?
Henry Gomez: Trace shows kernel selection happened after routing because compilation metadata didn't match quantized layout for the fallback replica. We should publish kernel hints with model metadata in the routing table.
Raj Patel: For quick mitigation: rollback microbatch cap to 8 in eu-west canary, and throttle cross-region fallback for interactive routes. That will trade throughput for p99.
Maya Li: Agreed. Plan: rollback microbatch -> 8 (canary group) + add temporary routing rule: max_cross_region_fallbacks=2/minute per-tenant. Can we simulate impact?
Lex Chen: I'll run a sim overnight with realistic key skew and add kernel-hint propagation. Will report p95/p99 curves. Also add a canary that forces kernel-compatible variant on fallback.
infra-bot: [deploy] rollback: canary/microbatch-cap -> 8 | initiated by Maya Li | link: https://console.redwood/infradeploy/rollbacks/1957654321
Henry Gomez: Quick profiling snippet from the worst trace:
```
profile: sequence=128
kvcache: miss -> remote fetch (120ms)
runtime: kernel_swap: quant_gen -> quant_fallback (extra 240ms kernel exec)
queue: microbatch=16 -> max_wait=180ms
total extra = 540ms
```
Olivia Park: That matches the 1.3s p99: base 420 + extra ~540 + network + jitter.
Raj Patel: After rollback + throttle, expected p99 should drop under 600ms. We'll measure after canary stabilizes.
Maya Li: Can someone add a dashboard panel for "fallback-induced extra latency" (compute time difference between local-hit traces and fallback traces) and set alert at 700ms p99?
Lex Chen: On it. Will add panel and a short-lived alert.
Olivia Park: Also let's capture the top 5 KV keys that cause fanout; they might be hot tenants or multipart tasks.
Henry Gomez: Extracting keys now, will attach in the follow-up thread.
Maya Li: Thanks all. Priority is to get p99 down for interactive routes. We'll reconvene after sim and rollback results. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: [dashboard] latency-multiplexing-fallbacks: https://console.redwood/dashboards/latency-fallbacks/1957654321
Lex Chen: I'll post sim results tomorrow AM. If anyone wants to pair on kernel-hint schema, ping me.
Olivia Park: pinged. let's also document the regression root cause in the perf playbook.
Maya Li: Ack, adding to perf playbook and incidents. Closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
